sudan.summary: أعلن وزير المالية السوداني جبريل إبراهيم أن موازنة العام المالي 2027 تهدف إلى تنفيذ برامج الإصلاح الاقتصادي والاجتماعي، وتعزيز جهود التعافي وإعادة الإعمار. تتضمن الموازنة برامج للحماية الاجتماعية لتحسين معاش المواطنين وتوفير الخدمات الأساسية، بالإضافة إلى معالجة قضايا النازحين واللاجئين. تم تحديد أولويات الإنفاق الحكومي لتشمل تمويل المجهود الحربي، وتحقيق الأمن والاستقرار، وتوفير الخدمات الأساسية، في ظل الأزمات الاقتصادية المتزايدة مثل ارتفاع تكاليف المعيشة ونقص الوقود والمواصلات. جاء ذلك خلال اجتماع مشترك للقطاعات الوزارية، حيث تم استعراض موجهات الموازنة قبل رفعها إلى مجلس الوزراء للمصادقة عليها. كما أكد الاجتماع على أهمية تعزيز الشفافية والحوكمة الاقتصادية، وتطوير الشراكات مع القطاع الخاص المحلي والأجنبي، وتوسيع برامج التحول الرقمي لتحسين الأداء المؤسسي. تواجه الحكومة تحديات كبيرة لتحقيق التوازن بين الإنفاق العسكري ومتطلبات إعادة الإعمار.

ethiopia.title: IG Kanja Orders Additional Police Deployment to Moyale Amid Ethiopia Border Crisis
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: IG Kanja Orders Additional Police Deployment to Moyale Amid Ethiopia Border Crisis - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: IG Kanja Orders Additional Police Deployment to Moyale Amid Ethiopia Border Crisis 6 November 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) By Irene Mwangi Nairobi — Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered the deployment of additional police officers to Moyale, Marsabit County, amid growing security concerns over escalating violence in neighbouring Ethiopia that has forced thousands of people to flee across the border into Kenya. Kanja announced the reinforcement on Thursday, November 5, during a high-level security assessment in the border town, where he chaired a strategic meeting with regional security commanders to evaluate the situation and strengthen measures to prevent the conflict from spilling into Kenyan territory. The Inspector General directed security officers deployed in the area to remain on high alert and enhance surveillance to protect residents, their property and other people seeking refuge in the country. He assured Moyale residents that the National Police Service (NPS) was committed to safeguarding lives and maintaining stability despite the deteriorating security situation across the border. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Kanja also urged residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing timely and credible intelligence that could help detect and prevent potential security threats. During the visit, he toured one of the camps hosting families displaced by the violence, assuring them of enhanced security and coordinated humanitarian assistance in partnership with relief agencies. The visit came amid an influx of Ethiopian nationals fleeing deadly clashes in the border town of Moyale on the Ethiopian side, where fighting between communities linked to the Oromia and Somali regional administrations has triggered widespread displacement. The violence, which escalated in October, has been linked to a dispute over territorial administration and the establishment of a Somali regional government office and display of its flag in contested territory. The clashes have resulted in deaths, injuries and destruction of property, with reports of heavy gunfire and artillery exchanges forcing civilians, particularly women and children, to seek safety in Kenya. The crisis has raised concerns about the safety of communities living on the Kenyan side of the border, with reports of stray bullets and rocket-propelled grenades hitting residential areas. Reports indicate that several Kenyan families had also fled their homes following repeated incidents involving stray ammunition. Areas affected include Lami, Manyatta Heillu, Sessi and parts of Moyale town, where houses have reportedly been damaged by stray bullets and rocket-propelled grenades. The humanitarian situation has also worsened, with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) reporting on October 28 that up to 50,000 people had crossed into Kenya, although the figure remained subject to verification. The agency said many of those fleeing were women and children, with some accommodated in temporary shelters, including schools and churches, while others were staying with relatives and host communities. UNHCR, alongside other humanitarian agencies, has been mobilising emergency supplies, including food, clean water, shelter materials and essential household items. The agencies are seeking approximately Sh1.16 billion to support up to 50,000 displaced people over three months. The crisis has also disrupted cross-border trade, with trucks stranded and some businesses near the One-Stop Border Post temporarily closing amid fears of stray gunfire. Marsabit Governor Mohamud Ali has previously called for an immediate ceasefire and peaceful dialogue, warning that continued fighting could worsen the humanitarian crisis and threaten stability in the border region. Kanja was accompanied by Directorate of Criminal Investigations Director Mohammed Amin, General Service Unit Commandant Johanna Tonui and Kenya Police Service Director of Operations Philip Opiyo. Others present included Eastern Regional Commissioner Jacob Muganda, Eastern Region Police Commander Stephen Chebet, Eastern Region Administration Police Commander Michael Owino and Eastern Regional Criminal Investigations Officer Michael Sang. ethiopia.summary: Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered the deployment of additional police officers to Moyale, Marsabit County, due to escalating violence in neighboring Ethiopia, which has led to a significant influx of refugees into Kenya. This decision was made during a security assessment meeting on November 5, where Kanja emphasized the need for heightened vigilance among security personnel to protect residents and those seeking refuge. The violence in Ethiopia, linked to territorial disputes between communities, has resulted in numerous casualties and widespread displacement, with reports indicating that up to 50,000 people have crossed into Kenya. The humanitarian situation is dire, with many refugees lacking adequate shelter and basic necessities. Kanja assured residents of the National Police Service's commitment to maintaining stability and urged community cooperation in reporting security threats. The ongoing conflict has also disrupted cross-border trade, raising concerns about safety in the region.

ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: African Political Parties Summit Delegates Witness Addis Ababa's Urban Transformation - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: African Political Parties Summit Delegates Witness Addis Ababa's Urban Transformation 5 November 2026 Ethiopian News Agency (Addis Ababa) Addis Ababa — African Political Parties Summit delegates have toured Addis Ababa's major urban development projects, witnessing the Ethiopian capital's ongoing transformation into a modern, inclusive and more accessible city. Speaking at a reception hosted in their honor, Head of the Democracy Building Center Coordinator Office with the rank of Deputy Prime Minister and Prosperity Party Vice President Adam Farah described Addis Ababa as the political capital and beating heart of Africa, emphasizing its significance as a shared home for all Africans. "When you are in Addis Ababa, you are not visiting a foreign city; you are returning home, to the heart of Africa," he said. Adem underscored that Africa's strength lies in the bonds of fraternity, solidarity and closer cooperation among its peoples, stressing the importance of shared political visions and aspirations in advancing the continent's development and self-reliance. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines He also invited the delegates to experience Ethiopia's renowned hospitality and rich cultural heritage, expressing hope that the summit would produce meaningful and tangible outcomes toward building a prosperous and united Africa. Meanwhile, the delegates concluded a series of field visits across Addis Ababa, touring major streets, modern urban corridors, public spaces and development projects that are reshaping the capital's urban landscape. During the visits, they gained insights into Ethiopia's integrated urban corridor development approach, which combines improved infrastructure, pedestrian-friendly spaces, accessibility and modern urban planning to create more functional and livable urban environments. Through museum visits and presentations, participants also explored the different phases of Addis Ababa's urban development and the vision underpinning its ongoing transformation. The programme concluded with a cultural reception featuring traditional music, artistic performances and songs reflecting Ethiopia's rich cultural diversity and heritage. Delegates expressed admiration for the performances and the authenticity of Ethiopian culture. The visits and cultural activities formed part of the accompanying programme of the Second African Political Parties Summit, hosted in Addis Ababa under the theme: "Governing for Growth: Political Parties as Architects of Africa's Economic Future." ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Suspends the Reporter Indefinitely in Escalating Assault On Independent Media
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia Suspends the Reporter Indefinitely in Escalating Assault On Independent Media - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia Suspends the Reporter Indefinitely in Escalating Assault On Independent Media Andrys Stienstra / Pixabay (file photo). 5 November 2026 Committee to Protect Journalists (New York) Nairobi — The Committee to Protect Journalists calls on Ethiopian authorities to immediately lift the indefinite suspension of The Reporter, one of the country's oldest independent newspapers. In a November 2 statement, the regulatory Ethiopian Media Authority (EMA) accused the Amharic- and English-language editions of the newspaper and their digital platforms of repeatedly publishing reports that undermine national interests, damage Ethiopia's image, threaten national security, and violate journalistic ethics. It suspended the registration certificate of The Reporter's publisher, Media and Communication Center PLC, for an "indefinite period," under the 2021 media law. "Ethiopia's media regulator has become an instrument of censorship, using vague and sweeping allegations of threats to 'national interests' to systematically punish independent journalism," said CPJ Africa Program Coordinator Muthoki Mumo. "Ethiopian authorities should immediately reverse this punitive decision, stop weaponizing media regulations to suppress scrutiny, and end their relentless campaign to dismantle the free press." The EMA said The Reporter, which was established in 1996, disseminated "distorted information" that was "not balanced," based on "unconfirmed information," and had a "negative impact on foreign investment, tourism and diplomacy." The regulator said it had monitored the outlet's content for over a year and held repeated discussions with the publisher and editors-in-chief, including issuing a final warning prior to announcing the suspension. The authority did not mention any specific report to substantiate its allegations. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines The Reporter's Amharic-language newspaper. (Screenshot: Ethiopian Reporter/YouTube) Two days earlier, The Reporter published an editorial titled "Press Freedom Is Not A Luxury!" that criticized authorities for treating independent reporting as a national security threat and called for the release of all journalists held without charge or in violation of constitutional bail guarantees. In 2026, the EMA revoked authorization for the Addis Standard and Wazema Radio. This year, the Authority also revoked the credentials of journalists with Reuters news agency for six months while a 2025 ban on two Deutsche Welle journalists remains in place. Earlier this year, the Reporter Magazine's Bewket Abebe was detained for three days and Addis Standard's Yonas Kedir was held for a day. CPJ's November 5 email to the EMA requesting comment did not receive an immediate response. Read the original article on CPJ . The EMA accused the publication of disseminating unverified and distorted information that could harm Ethiopia's image and threaten national security. This suspension follows a year of monitoring the outlet's content and discussions with its management, culminating in a final warning before the suspension was enacted. The Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) condemned the EMA's actions, labeling them as censorship and an attack on independent journalism. The Reporter had recently published an editorial advocating for press freedom and criticizing the government's treatment of independent media as a national security threat. This suspension adds to a troubling trend in Ethiopia, where several media outlets and journalists have faced similar punitive measures in recent years.

ethiopia.title: Germany Cautions 'Any Escalation in the Horn of Africa Must Be Avoided'
ethiopia.content: East Africa: Germany Cautions 'Any Escalation in the Horn of Africa Must Be Avoided' - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français East Africa: Germany Cautions 'Any Escalation in the Horn of Africa Must Be Avoided' 5 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has warned that "any escalation in the Horn of Africa must be avoided," as Ethiopia's relations with neighboring Eritrea and Sudan deteriorate, reaffirming Berlin's support for stability in northern Ethiopia. "A stable Ethiopia is vital to the entire region. Any escalation in the Horn of Africa must be avoided. Germany continues to support efforts to promote stability in northern Ethiopia," Wadephul said in a phone call with Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos, according to a German Foreign Ministry readout dated October 4, 2026. The warning comes amid intensified diplomatic efforts to prevent a wider conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea , following renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia, reported federal troop movements toward the Eritrean border and tensions over Ethiopia's desire for sovereign access to the Red Sea . Earlier, the African Union has renewed mediation, while the United States and European Union have called for de-escalation and Russia has offered to host direct talks. Ethiopia's ties with Sudan have also sharply deteriorated, with both countries expelling diplomats and closing consulates. This week, Ethiopia ordered six Sudanese diplomatic staff to leave its consulate in Assosa, prompting Sudan to close Ethiopia's consulate in Gedaref and expel its diplomats . Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines The two countries have traded accusations of backing armed opposition groups. Sudan has accused Ethiopia of allowing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces to use its territory for drone attacks and lodged complaints with the UN and AU. Ethiopia denies supporting the RSF and accuses Sudan, Egypt and Eritrea of aiding Tigrayan forces involved in ongoing conflict with federal and allied forces. Each allegation has been denied by the accused countries. The diplomatic rupture unfolds amid Sudan's devastating civil war and Ethiopia's worsening domestic crises, raising concerns that overlapping conflicts and regional rivalries could trigger a broader confrontation. Sudanese officials have said they seek to avoid open war, while the United States and United Kingdom are reportedly pursuing back-channel efforts to ease tensions. ethiopia.title: Winning Wars, Losing Peace - Ethiopia's Unfinished Political Struggle for Lasting Stability
ethiopia.content: Ethiopia: Winning Wars, Losing Peace - Ethiopia's Unfinished Political Struggle for Lasting Stability - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Ethiopia: Winning Wars, Losing Peace - Ethiopia's Unfinished Political Struggle for Lasting Stability 5 November 2026 Addis Standard (Addis Ababa) Addis Abeba — In contrast to 2018, when Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed took office, many Ethiopians hoped the country was entering a new era of peace and development; unfortunately, today, Ethiopia faces a dangerous convergence of armed conflicts, expanding battlefronts, unresolved territorial disputes, competing political ambitions, and regional tensions. Together, these crises threaten national stability and the lives, livelihoods, and future of millions. As of October 2026, renewed confrontation in Tigray, continued fighting between federal forces and Fano groups in Amhara, and the insurgency in Oromia illustrate the scale of Ethiopia's challenge. Tensions with Eritrea have also revived fears of interstate conflict, while localized communal, territorial, and resource-related violence adds further pressure. Recent clashes in Moyale offer another reminder that insecurity can spread beyond the country's most widely reported battlefronts. If the strategy of the federal government is to ignore worsening conflicts in the hope that they will disappear on their own, that approach is unlikely to succeed. These crises will not resolve themselves without a coordinated, credible, and sustained peace effort. Limits of military solutions Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Political and ethnic grievances cannot be resolved by force alone. In asymmetric conflicts, a militarily stronger government may find it difficult to defeat armed movements that draw on local grievances, geography, and community networks. The experiences of Vietnam and Afghanistan demonstrate how prolonged wars can exhaust powerful states without producing a durable political settlement. These cases are not identical to Ethiopia's, but they underline a crucial lesson: battlefield advantage does not guarantee lasting peace. Furthermore, the primary purpose of a national army is to defend the country's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and independence against external aggression. A national army should be a symbol of unity, security, and national pride, serving all citizens regardless of ethnicity or political affiliation. Although maintaining law and order is the responsibility of appropriate civilian institutions, relying on military force to suppress domestic political grievances risks deepening divisions and undermining public trust. A truly national army protects the nation from external threats; it should not become a substitute for political dialogue or treat citizens as enemies. Human, economic and political cost Prolonged conflict tears apart families and communities, forces people away from their homes, interrupts education, and deepens mistrust across ethnic and political lines. Children lose years of schooling, young people face uncertain futures, and families are pushed into poverty, displacement, and long-term dependency. The trauma of violence and the loss of loved ones can endure long after the fighting stops. Repeated conflict normalizes hostility, weakens social cohesion, and turns peaceful coexistence into a generational challenge. Young fighters also pay a lasting price. Repeated exposure to death, injury, fear, displacement, and the loss of comrades can erode emotional resilience. War fatigue may appear as exhaustion, disillusionment, emotional numbness, anxiety, or difficulty imagining life beyond the battlefield. Its effects can continue after demobilization, complicating family relationships, employment, and reintegration into civilian life. When war continues without a credible political solution, a generation risks losing not only its youth, education, and productive years, but also its psychological well-being and confidence in the future. Recognizing war fatigue is not weakness; it is a reminder that young people must not be treated as expendable instruments of political ambition. Sustainable peace must offer a realistic path to safety, healing, education, work, dignity, and meaningful participation in rebuilding the country. Ethiopia's greatest challenge is not merely to end today's wars but to build a political order in which future wars become less necessary, less attractive, and less likely." The economic and political damage is equally severe. Insecurity disrupts farming and trade, destroys productive assets, discourages investment, and squeezes household incomes and public finances. Money spent on prolonged military operations is money unavailable for schools, hospitals, infrastructure, agricultural development, and jobs. Politically, persistent warfare erodes public confidence in institutions and reinforces the belief that power is won through force rather than public consent and the rule of law. Emergency conditions can weaken oversight and create opportunities for corruption while institutional reform is postponed. Ethiopia risks losing not only lives and economic progress but also the trust and accountability needed for a stable democratic state. Political disputes require political solutions Poorly managed ethnic federalism, combined with unresolved regional boundaries, can create dangerous conditions for future conflict in Ethiopia. When political representation, access to land and resources, administrative authority, and regional identity become closely tied to ethnicity, disputes over where communities belong and which region controls a contested area can quickly become politically charged. These issues risk becoming time bombs--not because ethnic diversity or federalism must inevitably lead to violence, but because unresolved grievances can be exploited when institutions lack the trust and legitimacy needed to manage them peacefully. Grand buildings and bright city lights may project an image of progress in Addis Abeba, but Addis Aeaba is not Ethiopia. National development cannot be measured by the capital's skyline while communities elsewhere live with insecurity, displacement, closed schools, disrupted livelihoods, and fear. Visible construction cannot substitute for peace, justice, accountable government, and citizens' confidence that their grievances can be addressed without taking up arms. Ethiopia's political leadership, opposition movements, regional authorities, and armed organizations face a fundamental choice: continue pursuing political objectives primarily through force or build credible mechanisms to negotiate differences. That requires serious engagement, realistic compromise, protection of civilians, and a willingness to address legitimate grievances without treating every disagreement as a security threat. Peace negotiations must be sustained and purposeful--not symbolic exercises or temporary pauses while parties prepare for the next round of fighting. True victory is measured not only by battlefield gains but also by whether adversaries can move beyond confrontation toward a sustainable peace. When continued fighting imposes unbearable costs on both sides without offering a lasting solution, negotiation becomes the wiser and more courageous strategy. Successful negotiation is not a sign of weakness or surrender; it is an exercise in strategic leadership. Through dialogue, compromise, mutual recognition, and carefully negotiated guarantees, former adversaries can protect essential interests, address legitimate concerns, and establish a foundation for coexistence. A genuine win-win outcome does not require either side to obtain everything it wants. It requires each side to recognize that a fair, workable settlement may secure more of what matters than another round of war. Ethiopia's greatest challenge is not merely to end today's wars but to build a political order in which future wars become less necessary, less attractive, and less likely. That demands leadership capable of placing the country's survival and the well-being of its people above short-term political advantage. Without that commitment, the end of one war may be only an interval before the next. As of October 2026, renewed violence in Tigray, ongoing clashes in Amhara, and insurgencies in Oromia highlight the country's precarious situation. Tensions with Eritrea and localized violence further exacerbate the crisis, threatening millions' lives and livelihoods. The government's reliance on military solutions risks deepening divisions and undermining public trust, as prolonged conflict disrupts education and economic stability. Home News IG Kanja Orders Deployment of More Police Officers to Moyale Amid Ethiopia Tensions IG Kanja Orders Deployment of More Police Officers to Moyale Amid Ethiopia Tensions Nov 06, 2026 at 07:00 AM | By Kevin Koech Deployment File image of the Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja Share This Story WhatsApp Facebook X Telegram LinkedIn Editor's Review IG of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered the deployment of additional police officers to Moyale to reinforce security amid growing tensions and insecurity in Ethiopia. Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja has ordered the deployment of additional police officers to Moyale, Marsabit County, to reinforce security amid growing tensions and insecurity in neighbouring Ethiopia. Kanja conducted an extensive security assessment in Moyale on Thursday, November 5, where he met regional security officials to evaluate the security situation and discuss measures to safeguard residents. Join our WhatsApp Channel for the latest news updates. During the visit, the Inspector General chaired a strategic meeting with regional security officials, focusing on the emerging security developments across the border and their potential implications for the safety of communities in the area. The National Police Service said the additional deployment was intended to strengthen existing security operations and improve the capacity of officers to prevent and respond to potential threats. Read More Sifuna Raises Alarm Over Covert Police Units in Missing Lawyer Case Murkomen, IG Kanja Sued Over Political Violence Ahead of 2027 Elections NPS Addresses Viral Statement on Alleged Abduction of Tanzanian Activist Twaha Mwaipaya "To bolster defensive and preventive capabilities, the Inspector General announced the deployment of additional police officers to reinforce existing security. "He firmly assured the residents of Moyale of the National Police Service's unwavering commitment to protecting their lives and property," the NPS said. File image of Douglas Kanja in Moyale Kanja urged security personnel deployed to the region to remain alert and maintain high levels of vigilance as they continued carrying out their duties. He also called on residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing timely information that could help officers address security threats and maintain stability. "The IG further encouraged residents to work closely with security agencies by sharing timely and relevant information and to continue maintaining peace," the NPS added. As part of his visit, Kanja also toured one of the camps hosting families displaced by the insecurity, where he assured them of enhanced protection. He further pledged coordinated humanitarian assistance for the displaced populations in collaboration with relief partners, as security agencies continued monitoring developments in the region. Elsewhere, the death toll from the building collapse in Eastleigh, Nairobi, has risen to eight after six more bodies were recovered from the rubble on Thursday, November 5. In a statement, the NPS said multi-agency response teams were continuing search, rescue and recovery operations at the site of the incident, which occurred on October 23, 2026. The latest recovery brought the number of people confirmed dead to eight, while four others had been rescued alive since the building collapsed. "The teams remain on the ground, working in coordination to reach areas beneath the rubble and account for all those who may have been caught in the collapse," the statement read. The National Police Service disclosed that the six bodies recovered on Thursday belonged to four women and two men. NPS expressed condolences to families who lost their loved ones in the tragedy and urged those searching for missing relatives to seek assistance through the Kenya Red Cross team stationed at the scene. "We continue to support the multi-agency operation and call on members of the public to sustain their cooperation by keeping away from the affected site, following guidance from response teams, and allowing emergency personnel unhindered access," the statement added. ethiopia.title: Ethiopia Becomes Africa's Fifth-Largest Economy After Rebasing GDP
ethiopia.content: Africa: Ethiopia Becomes Africa's Fifth-Largest Economy After Rebasing GDP - allAfrica.com AllAfrica English (current) En Français Toggle navigation My Account Toggle navigation AllAfrica My Account English (current) En Français Africa: Ethiopia Becomes Africa's Fifth-Largest Economy After Rebasing GDP 5 November 2026 Daba Finance (Abidjan) Ethiopia has become Africa's fifth-largest economy after revising its gross domestic product figures to account for sectors including digital finance, services and manufacturing. The country's economy was valued at $210.7 billion in the fiscal year ended July 2026, Finance Minister Fitsum Assefa announced on November 4. The revision places Ethiopia behind South Africa, Egypt, Nigeria and Algeria, and ahead of Morocco and Kenya, based on available GDP estimates. The country previously ranked outside Africa's 5 largest economies. The government updated the base year used to calculate GDP from 2015-16 to 2024-25, increasing the estimated size of the economy in the new base year by 59.2% to $201.4 billion from approximately $126.4 billion. In local currency, GDP for 2024-25 was revised to 24.03 trillion birr from 15.09 trillion birr. The revised figures put output at 31.86 trillion birr in 2025-26. Officials said the previous calculations no longer reflected changes in the country's economic structure, including growth in digital services, financial technology and other activities. The revision incorporates information from an agricultural census, household surveys and data from state-owned enterprises and nonprofit institutions. Services now account for almost 36% of Ethiopia's GDP, making them the largest contributor to economic output. Agriculture represents approximately 32%, while industry accounts for 30%. The services sector includes transport, telecommunications, banking and aviation, with Ethiopian Airlines contributing to economic activity through passenger and cargo operations. The higher GDP estimate could improve Ethiopia's reported debt indicators as the government continues restructuring its external obligations under the G20 Common Framework. A larger economy reduces debt as a percentage of GDP without changing the amount owed. Oxford Economics said the revision could improve headline debt sustainability measures, although debt repayments, foreign currency requirements and interest costs remain unchanged. The new figures could also affect calculations used by lenders, investors and international financial institutions to assess the country's finances. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Ethiopia, Africa's second-most populous country, expects economic growth of 10.2% in the fiscal year ending July 2027. The government has introduced reforms aimed at attracting foreign investment, including opening parts of the telecommunications and banking sectors to international companies. Authorities also moved to a market-based exchange rate in 2024 under an economic reform programme supported by the International Monetary Fund. The GDP revision provides a new benchmark for measuring economic performance, government revenue and debt, although the country's ranking will depend on future growth and exchange-rate movements. Key Takeaways Ethiopia's rise to become Africa's fifth-largest economy shows how changes in national accounting methods can affect economic rankings without creating new output. The government's decision to update its GDP base year from 2015-16 to 2024-25 increased the estimated size of the economy by 59.2%, reflecting activities that were missing or underrepresented in earlier calculations. The revision places Ethiopia's GDP at $210.7 billion for 2025-26, ahead of Morocco and Kenya under the reported comparison. However, the increase does not mean Ethiopia produced 59.2% more goods and services overnight. Instead, the revised figures provide a different measurement of activity already taking place in the economy. The change could have implications for government finances because GDP is used to calculate debt ratios, tax revenue ratios and fiscal deficits. A larger GDP figure lowers the reported debt-to-GDP ratio even when the amount of debt remains unchanged. This may improve some indicators used by creditors and investors, but it does not reduce interest payments or foreign currency obligations. The revision could also lower measured tax revenue as a percentage of GDP, highlighting the need to expand government revenue collection. Ethiopia's economy remains dependent on agriculture and services, which together account for approximately 68% of output. Reforms involving telecommunications, banking and foreign exchange markets could create opportunities for investors as the country opens sectors that previously faced restrictions. However, Ethiopia continues to face challenges involving debt restructuring, currency availability, inflation and infrastructure investment. For investors, the next indicators will be economic growth, foreign direct investment, government revenue, export earnings and progress in debt negotiations. The revised GDP figures improve the measurement of Ethiopia's economy, but sustained growth and stronger public finances will determine whether its higher ranking translates into improved economic conditions. The Finance Minister announced that the economy was valued at $210.7 billion for the fiscal year ending July 2026, marking a 59.2% increase from previous estimates. This revision places Ethiopia behind South Africa, Egypt, Nigeria, and Algeria, while surpassing Morocco and Kenya. Services now contribute nearly 36% to the GDP, with agriculture and industry following closely. border point. [File, Standard] Escalating violence along the Kenya-Ethiopia border has reached a critical threshold, demanding immediate and decisive action. What began as a localised territorial dispute has rapidly expanded into a cross-border security and humanitarian crisis that Kenya can no longer treat as a mere foreign quarrel. At least three Kenyans have been killed and about 20 wounded by gunfire and munitions crossing from Ethiopia. The latest victim, 65-year-old Amina Guchi, was struck by a stray bullet at the county offices in Moyale on Monday. On the Ethiopian side, a hospital official counted nine dead within days of the fighting, while other accounts speak of scores, with a 13-year-old girl among the first to die. Compounding this volatile situation, a shocking escalation occurred on Tuesday when 300 heavily armed Nyagatom warriors from Ethiopia launched an attack on the Kibish watering point in Turkana North. During the siege, a police reservist was injured while attempting to defend local pastoralists. This is an aggressive breach of territorial sovereignty. Criminal elements and armed militias are exploiting the regional instability to launch unprovoked incursions into Kenya. These deaths in Moyale stem from a long-standing dispute between Ethiopia's Oromia and Somali regional administrations over a town both claim. Tensions escalated sharply on October 18, when the Somali region's flag was reportedly raised over a contested office. Since about October 22, forces from both sides have exchanged heavy fire, and the fighting has spread to neighbouring districts. The impact of these conflicts on Kenya has been serious. Rocket-propelled grenades have landed in Kenyan communities, schools near the Moyale border have been disrupted, and two examination centres had to be relocated. Simultaneously, the United Nations estimates that more than 50,000 Ethiopians have crossed into Marsabit County, placing severe strain on local water, food, shelter, and sanitation infrastructure. The Kenyan government should respond firmly. It should bolster security along the Kenya-Ethiopia border —from the troubled stretches of Moyale down to the remote reaches of Turkana North—including by deploying the Kenya Defence Forces. The security personnel should clear unexploded ordnance, repel armed raiders, and protect vulnerable residents and learners within range of the guns. Furthermore, humanitarian agencies must be fully supported to shelter and feed the displaced before hunger and disease compound the tragedy. Security measures alone, however, will not end the suffering. Only dialogue will. Ethiopia's federal authorities must step up, rein in the forces of both regions. The African Union, IGAD, and the United Nations must take the lead rather than follow events, pressing for an immediate ceasefire, facilitating regional mediation, and initiating an independent inquiry into the killings. Each day of delay is measured in civilian lives on both sides of the border. Support Independent Journalism Stand With Bold Journalism. Stand With The Standard . ethiopia.summary: Escalating violence along the Kenya-Ethiopia border has prompted urgent calls for enhanced security measures. The conflict, initially a localized territorial dispute, has evolved into a humanitarian crisis, resulting in multiple casualties on both sides. Recent incidents include the death of a 65-year-old Kenyan woman from stray gunfire and an attack by armed Ethiopian warriors on a Kenyan watering point, highlighting the severity of the situation. The ongoing clashes have disrupted local communities, with rocket-propelled grenades landing in Kenyan areas and over 50,000 Ethiopians seeking refuge in Marsabit County, straining resources. The Kenyan government is urged to deploy the Kenya Defence Forces to secure the border and protect civilians. Additionally, dialogue is essential for a lasting resolution, with calls for Ethiopian authorities and international organizations to facilitate ceasefire negotiations and address the root causes of the conflict. Immediate humanitarian support is also critical to assist displaced individuals and prevent further suffering.

ethiopia.title: Somalia warns Ethiopia unrest could weaken AUSSOM security operations - Hiiraan Online
ethiopia.content: Somalia warns Ethiopia unrest could weaken AUSSOM security operations - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME SECURITY Somalia warns Ethiopia unrest could weaken AUSSOM security operations Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Thursday November 5, 2026 Mogadishu (HOL) - Somalia warned Thursday that worsening political and security instability in neighboring Ethiopia could affect security operations inside Somalia, including the African Union mission fighting al-Shabab. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar Balcad, told TRT World that Ethiopia’s stability was directly linked to Somalia’s security because of the countries’ long shared border and deep economic, social and historical ties. advertisements He warned that prolonged unrest inside Ethiopia could affect Ethiopian troops serving in the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), potentially forcing Addis Ababa to reduce or withdraw forces to respond to domestic security pressures. Ethiopian troops remain a significant component of AUSSOM. The African Union approved a contingent of about 2,500 Ethiopian troops for the mission, alongside forces from Uganda, Kenya, Djibouti and Egypt. Ethiopia has also deployed additional forces in Somalia under bilateral arrangements. The African Union Peace and Security Council praised both Ethiopia and Uganda in February for sending additional troops as a temporary measure to address Somalia’s security situation. In September, the Ethiopian National Defence Force completed a major rotation of troops serving in AUSSOM’s Sector 4, which covers parts of central Somalia. New Ethiopian personnel replaced troops stationed in Beletweyne and Halgan after a three-year deployment. Ali Balcad cautioned that a deterioration of Ethiopia’s internal security could therefore have consequences for Somalia if Ethiopian forces were required to redeploy home or became less able to support operations against al-Shabab. Such a development could create additional pressure on Somali security forces at a time when the federal government and AUSSOM are already trying to gradually transfer responsibility for national security to Somali institutions. The warning comes amid renewed fighting inside Ethiopia. Conflict between Ethiopia’s federal government and forces linked to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front erupted again in September, effectively breaking down the 2022 Pretoria peace agreement that ended a devastating two-year war. Ethiopian government forces later retook much of Tigray, including the regional capital, Mekelle. Violence has also continued in Amhara. Drone strikes on a displacement camp there killed at least 15 people, including children, on Oct. 30, according to people involved in rescue efforts who spoke to Reuters. It was not clear who carried out the attack. Regional tensions have also increased between Ethiopia and Eritrea, with the two countries severing diplomatic relations and reports of Eritrean troops entering northern Ethiopia during the renewed Tigray fighting. Ali Balcad also warned that violence inside Ethiopia could directly affect ethnic Somalis living in Ethiopia’s Somali Region, which borders Somalia. AUSSOM replaced the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia at the beginning of 2025. Its mandate includes supporting Somali forces in operations against al-Shabab, protecting key population centers and infrastructure, and helping Somali security institutions assume greater responsibility for national security. The African Union has repeatedly warned that any changes to the mission must be carefully coordinated to prevent security gaps, particularly while al-Shabab retains the ability to carry out major attacks across southern and central Somalia. ethiopia.summary: Somalia has expressed concerns that escalating unrest in Ethiopia could jeopardize security operations within its borders, particularly those involving the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM). State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar Balcad emphasized the interconnectedness of the two nations' security, citing their extensive border and historical ties. He warned that ongoing instability in Ethiopia might compel the Ethiopian government to withdraw troops from AUSSOM to address domestic issues, thereby weakening efforts against the militant group al-Shabab. Ethiopian forces play a crucial role in AUSSOM, which includes around 2,500 troops from Ethiopia, Uganda, Kenya, Djibouti, and Egypt. The warning comes amid renewed violence in Ethiopia, particularly in the Tigray and Amhara regions, raising fears for ethnic Somalis in Ethiopia's Somali Region. Balcad highlighted the need for coordinated efforts to prevent security gaps as Somalia transitions to greater national security responsibility.

This was stated by Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja during a visit to Kenya’s Moyale, Nation Kenya reports . Fighting between forces from Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regions has been ongoing for two weeks. It has forced thousands of Ethiopians to seek safety in Kenya, while stray bullets and rocket-propelled grenades have also forced dozens of Kenyan families near the border to leave their homes. Affected areas and evacuation The areas of Somare, Sessi, Biashara, Lami and Geillu have been most affected by stray munitions. The previous day, two people were injured by stray gunfire, with one incident occurring near Moyale Police Station. During nighttime fighting on the Ethiopian side of the border in the Lami area, bullets damaged houses and a vehicle. More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram . Kanja also announced plans to allocate more resources and personnel to protect Kenyan territory. According to him, the authorities seek to safely evacuate truck drivers and other Kenyan citizens stranded in Ethiopia. Local residents said that several drivers returning to Kenya have been unable to leave the Moyale–Addis Ababa highway for two weeks. The number of displaced people is rising The inspector general visited a temporary shelter for displaced Ethiopians at OMC School, where he promised to strengthen security. He also met with local elders and humanitarian organizations assisting people who have left their homes. According to Malik Adan, head of the Kenya Red Cross in the Upper Eastern region, the number of displaced people has risen from 36,000 to more than 50,000. Mohamed Guio, deputy chair of the Moyale cross-border committee, called on security agencies to step up patrols to prevent the conflict from spreading into Kenyan territory. The conflict, which has been raging for two weeks between Ethiopian forces from the Oromia and Somali regions, has led to thousands of Ethiopians fleeing to Kenya for safety. somalia.summary: Somalia's political crisis intensified on Thursday when the Supreme Court rejected President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's attempt to extend his term. The court's ruling has raised concerns about the stability of the government and the potential for increased tensions among political factions. The president's term extension was seen by many as a move to consolidate power amid ongoing challenges, including security issues and humanitarian crises. The decision has sparked reactions from various political leaders and civil society groups, who are calling for adherence to constitutional processes and democratic norms. As the political landscape becomes more volatile, there are fears that this ruling could lead to further unrest and complicate efforts to achieve peace and stability in the country. The situation remains fluid, with stakeholders urging dialogue and cooperation to navigate the ongoing crisis.

somalia.summary: Somalia is experiencing a deepening political crisis as President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud faces accusations of unlawfully arresting the Supreme Court's chief justice. This turmoil follows the court's declaration that Mohamud's extension of his presidential term, which he announced during a "transition period," was illegal. The situation has escalated tensions between the government and opposition factions, leading to violent clashes amid ongoing challenges from the Islamist group Al-Shabaab. Mohamud has aimed to transition Somalia towards democratic elections, moving away from a clan-based political system. However, the recent actions against the judiciary have raised concerns about the rule of law and the government's legitimacy, further complicating the country's efforts to stabilize and gain international support. The unfolding events highlight the fragile state of Somalia's political landscape and the potential for increased unrest.

somalia.title: Somalia warns Ethiopia unrest could weaken AUSSOM security operations - Hiiraan Online
somalia.content: Somalia warns Ethiopia unrest could weaken AUSSOM security operations - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME SECURITY Somalia warns Ethiopia unrest could weaken AUSSOM security operations Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Thursday November 5, 2026 Mogadishu (HOL) - Somalia warned Thursday that worsening political and security instability in neighboring Ethiopia could affect security operations inside Somalia, including the African Union mission fighting al-Shabab. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar Balcad, told TRT World that Ethiopia’s stability was directly linked to Somalia’s security because of the countries’ long shared border and deep economic, social and historical ties. advertisements He warned that prolonged unrest inside Ethiopia could affect Ethiopian troops serving in the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), potentially forcing Addis Ababa to reduce or withdraw forces to respond to domestic security pressures. Ethiopian troops remain a significant component of AUSSOM. The African Union approved a contingent of about 2,500 Ethiopian troops for the mission, alongside forces from Uganda, Kenya, Djibouti and Egypt. Ethiopia has also deployed additional forces in Somalia under bilateral arrangements. The African Union Peace and Security Council praised both Ethiopia and Uganda in February for sending additional troops as a temporary measure to address Somalia’s security situation. In September, the Ethiopian National Defence Force completed a major rotation of troops serving in AUSSOM’s Sector 4, which covers parts of central Somalia. New Ethiopian personnel replaced troops stationed in Beletweyne and Halgan after a three-year deployment. Ali Balcad cautioned that a deterioration of Ethiopia’s internal security could therefore have consequences for Somalia if Ethiopian forces were required to redeploy home or became less able to support operations against al-Shabab. Such a development could create additional pressure on Somali security forces at a time when the federal government and AUSSOM are already trying to gradually transfer responsibility for national security to Somali institutions. The warning comes amid renewed fighting inside Ethiopia. Conflict between Ethiopia’s federal government and forces linked to the Tigray People’s Liberation Front erupted again in September, effectively breaking down the 2022 Pretoria peace agreement that ended a devastating two-year war. Ethiopian government forces later retook much of Tigray, including the regional capital, Mekelle. Violence has also continued in Amhara. Drone strikes on a displacement camp there killed at least 15 people, including children, on Oct. 30, according to people involved in rescue efforts who spoke to Reuters. It was not clear who carried out the attack. Regional tensions have also increased between Ethiopia and Eritrea, with the two countries severing diplomatic relations and reports of Eritrean troops entering northern Ethiopia during the renewed Tigray fighting. Ali Balcad also warned that violence inside Ethiopia could directly affect ethnic Somalis living in Ethiopia’s Somali Region, which borders Somalia. AUSSOM replaced the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia at the beginning of 2025. Its mandate includes supporting Somali forces in operations against al-Shabab, protecting key population centers and infrastructure, and helping Somali security institutions assume greater responsibility for national security. The African Union has repeatedly warned that any changes to the mission must be carefully coordinated to prevent security gaps, particularly while al-Shabab retains the ability to carry out major attacks across southern and central Somalia. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Ali Mohamed Omar Balcad emphasized the interconnectedness of the two nations' security, citing their extensive border and historical ties. He warned that ongoing instability in Ethiopia might compel the Ethiopian government to withdraw troops from AUSSOM to address domestic issues, thereby weakening efforts against the militant group al-Shabab. Ethiopian forces play a crucial role in AUSSOM, which includes around 2,500 troops from Ethiopia, Uganda, Kenya, Djibouti, and Egypt. somalia.title: Somalia rejects Israeli ambassador to Somaliland and planned embassy in Hargeisa - Hiiraan Online
somalia.content: Somalia rejects Israeli ambassador to Somaliland and planned embassy in Hargeisa - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME POLITICS Somalia rejects Israeli ambassador to Somaliland and planned embassy in Hargeisa Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ Wednesday November 4, 2026 Mogadishu (HOL) — Somalia rejected Israel’s accreditation of an ambassador to Somaliland and the laying of a cornerstone for a planned embassy in Hargeisa, calling the moves violations of its sovereignty and territorial integrity. The Foreign Ministry said Tuesday that the steps had been taken without the consent of Somalia’s federal government and declared them “null and void and without legal effect.” advertisements Israel’s first ambassador to Somaliland, Michael Lotem, presented his credentials to Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi Irro in Hargeisa last week, Israel’s Foreign Ministry announced Sunday. A cornerstone ceremony for a future Israeli embassy followed. “These actions, undertaken without the consent of the Federal Government of Somalia, constitute a flagrant violation of Somalia’s sovereignty, territorial integrity and unity,” Somalia’s Foreign Ministry said. Mogadishu maintains that Somaliland remains an integral part of Somalia and argues that it cannot independently establish diplomatic missions with foreign states. The ministry cited the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, arguing that the establishment of diplomatic relations and permanent missions requires the consent of the sovereign state. Somaliland declared independence from Somalia in 1991 and has governed itself for more than three decades with its own institutions, security forces and currency. Somalia rejects its claim to independence. Israel formally recognized Somaliland on Dec. 26, 2025, becoming the first U.N. member state to do so since Somaliland’s 1991 declaration. No other U.N. member state has followed. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar described the exchange of ambassadors as fulfillment of commitments made when the two sides established diplomatic relations and said Israel intended to deepen ties with Somaliland. Somaliland officials have welcomed the relationship and described the credential ceremony and planned embassy as milestones in expanding cooperation with Israel in areas including trade, security, technology and investment. Somalia, however, said Israel’s latest actions compounded what it described as the unlawful recognition of Somaliland. The African Union, Arab League, Organization of Islamic Cooperation and other regional bodies have previously rejected Israel’s recognition move and reaffirmed support for Somalia’s territorial integrity. “At a time of heightened insecurity in the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden, actions that encourage fragmentation and disregard internationally recognised borders risk deepening tensions across an already fragile region,” Somalia’s Foreign Ministry said. Mogadishu demanded that Israel reverse the measures and called on governments and international organizations not to take steps that could confer legitimacy on them. The federal government also said it reserved the right to pursue diplomatic, political and legal measures under international law in defense of Somalia’s sovereignty and territorial integrity. The Somali Foreign Ministry stated that these developments occurred without the federal government's consent, rendering them "null and void." somalia.content: Somalia’s Supreme Court overrules presidential term extension - The EastAfrican Today's Paper | Our Brands Home East Africa Southern Africa Central Africa West Africa North Africa World Africa Eastern Africa More ••• Sign in My Account Personal details Change password Purchases Sign out Search Home News East Africa Southern Africa Central Africa West Africa North Africa World Africa Eastern Africa Business & Tech Opinion Columnists Editorials Cartoon Guest Blogs Sustainability Innovation Health Climate Magazine Services Today's Paper Our Brands Prime Somalia’s Supreme Court overrules presidential term extension Thursday, November 05, 2026 - 3 min read Somalia President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. Photo credit: Reuters By Aggrey Mutambo & Abdulkadir Khalif Thank you for reading businessdailyafrica.com Show plans Somalia’s Supreme Court on Thursday overruled a presidential term extension that had been announced earlier, creating uncertainty regarding President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s tenure. However, the statement, which was endorsed by five of the nine judges, came a day after President Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed amid disputes over his independence. The five judges instead issued a directive that Somalia’s political leaders must work out an electoral plan within 30 days and conduct elections within 90 days. Related East Africa Somalia’s election dispute reaches Supreme Court amid deepening political crisis Oct 29 - 4 min read East Africa PRIME Somalia election timetable deepens political divisions Oct 16 - 4 min read This followed a lawsuit filed by a group of opposition leaders, led by former president Sheikh Sharif Ahmed, to stop constitutional amendments that Mohamud had relied on to extend his and parliament’s term by a year, and the federal parliament’s decision to extend the tenure of elected officials from four to five years. These changes have been controversial and have damaged Mogadishu’s relations with some federal states, such as Jubaland and Puntland. They are also the reason why Somalia is embroiled in disputes over an electoral calendar or model of elections. The five judges did not invalidate the amendments made in March this year. However, they ruled that the term extensions for parliament in April and the presidency in May were illegal. The presidency will now operate as a caretaker administration pending an electoral agreement and subsequent elections. Five judges endorsed this decision, although two others were present when it was delivered. The court usually has nine judges, but a sitting is valid if five judges are present. However, Chief Justice Ahmed, who usually presides over sittings, had been dismissed the previous day. He is embroiled in a political dispute with the president. His whereabouts were unknown when the decision was delivered on Thursday. The judges also rejected the decision to fire their Chief Justice, which was announced on the Presidency’s social media accounts on Wednesday. This signalled the growing animosity between the two institutions. It remains to be seen whether the decision could provide opposition groups with more ammunition with which to target the President. However, it could still escalate the tension between the two sides, who disagree on the electoral model. The opposition has called for the old constitution to be reinstated, rejecting any term extensions. The Presidency insists that elections must be held next year under universal suffrage rather than the clan collegiate system. Last month, the electoral commission issued a calendar of events indicating that elections should be held by May next year. Opposition groups rejected this. somalia.summary: Somalia’s Supreme Court has overruled a controversial presidential term extension announced by President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, creating uncertainty about his administration. The court's decision, supported by five of the nine judges, mandates that political leaders devise an electoral plan within 30 days and conduct elections within 90 days. This ruling follows a lawsuit from opposition leaders, including former president Sheikh Sharif Ahmed, challenging the constitutional amendments that allowed the term extensions. While the court did not invalidate the amendments made in March, it deemed the extensions for both the presidency and parliament illegal. The ruling has intensified tensions between the presidency and the judiciary, especially after Mohamud dismissed Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed just a day prior. The opposition continues to reject the proposed electoral model, advocating for the reinstatement of the old constitution. The situation remains fluid as the country grapples with political disputes and the need for a clear electoral process.

somalia.summary: Uganda has initiated the withdrawal of its troops from Somalia, marking a significant shift in its foreign security commitment. The Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF) has been stationed in Somalia since March 2007, becoming the first foreign military to intervene in the country, which was then plagued by clan warfare. Currently, approximately 4,500 troops are part of the African Union (AU) mission in Somalia, supplemented by around 2,000 additional troops through bilateral agreements. The withdrawal raises questions about the future security landscape in Somalia, particularly regarding the stability and effectiveness of local forces in the absence of UPDF support. As Uganda begins this exit, the implications for Somalia's ongoing conflict and the broader regional security dynamics remain uncertain, prompting discussions on the next steps for both Somalia and the international community involved in peacekeeping efforts.

somalia.title: Somalia's supreme court rules the extension of presidential and parliamentary terms is unconstitutional - ConstitutionNet
somalia.content: Somalia's supreme court rules the extension of presidential and parliamentary terms is unconstitutional | ConstitutionNet Skip to main content Newsletters Subscribe Menu Home About ConstitutionNet Constitutions FAQ Glossary About ConstitutionNet Constitutions FAQ Glossary News Constitutions in the News Voices from the Field News Constitutions in the News Voices from the Field Countries Resources Publications Tools & Databases Primers Documents Resources Publications Tools & Databases Event Series Documents You are reading: News Somalia's supreme court rules the extension of presidential and parliamentary terms is unconstitutional Constitutional Court/Judical Review Constitutional Amendment Regulation and Accountability Africa Somalia 5 November 2026 Flag of Somalia (photo credit: David_Peterson via pixabay) Somalia’s Supreme Court ruled Thursday that the constitutional mandates of the federal parliament, president and government expired in 2026, declaring actions taken by the institutions after the end of their terms unconstitutional and legally invalid. [ . . . ] The court rejected the first part of Sharif’s petition, which challenged the constitutionality of the amendment process, ruling that the former president lacked the legal standing to bring the case under Article 86 of the Provisional Constitution. However, it accepted the second part, which questioned the legality of measures arising from the constitutional changes, particularly the extension of the mandates of elected federal institutions. In its ruling, the court said constitutional amendments introducing new terms of office must explicitly state whether the changes apply to institutions already in office or only to those elected afterward. Where an amendment does not clearly address the issue, the new term cannot automatically be applied to sitting institutions, and their original mandates remain in force, the court said. somalia.summary: Somalia's Supreme Court has ruled that the extension of presidential and parliamentary terms is unconstitutional, declaring that the mandates of the federal parliament, president, and government expired in 2026. The court's decision invalidates any actions taken by these institutions after their terms ended. While the court dismissed a challenge from former President Sharif regarding the amendment process's constitutionality, it upheld the argument questioning the legality of the extended mandates. The ruling emphasized that constitutional amendments must explicitly state their applicability to existing institutions; otherwise, the original terms remain in effect. This landmark decision reinforces the importance of adhering to constitutional provisions and clarifies the legal standing of elected officials in Somalia. The ruling is a significant step in upholding constitutional integrity in the country.

football.summary: تعادل فريق الهلال السوداني مع رايون سبورت الرواندي بنتيجة 1-1 في مباراة أقيمت يوم 4 نوفمبر 2026، ضمن الجولة السابعة من الدوري الرواندي. رغم البداية القوية بتسجيل قائد الفريق محمد عبد الرحمن هدف التقدم، إلا أن الهلال أهدر فرصة الفوز بعد أن أدرك المنافس التعادل في اللحظات الأخيرة. هذا التعادل أحبط جماهير الهلال، لكنه يحمل بعض المكاسب، حيث عزز عبد الرحمن سجله التهديفي، مما يعزز فرصه في المباريات المقبلة، خاصة في دوري أبطال أفريقيا. المدرب جوزيف زينباور يخطط لاستغلال فترة التوقف الدولي لإجراء مباريات ودية، حيث سيلتحق 16 لاعباً من الهلال بمنتخباتهم الوطنية. بعد فترة التوقف، سيواجه الهلال حوريا كوناكري الغيني في 28 نوفمبر، ثم المغرب الفاسي وبيراميدز المصري، مما يتطلب تجهيز الفريق بشكل جيد لتحقيق نتائج إيجابية.

أبطال أفريقيا الهلال السوداني مصطفى كرشوم الدوري السوداني الممتاز كرة قدم حافظ محمد أحمد الخرطوم winwin أضفنا الى 'غوغل' وصف الألماني جوزيف زينباور مدرب الهلال السوداني، نتيجة التعادل (1-1) التي حققها فريقه أمام رايون سبورت الرواندي في الجولة السابعة من مسابقة الدوري الرواندي بالسيئة، مؤكدا أن فريقه فرط في فوز كان في المتناول بعد تقدمه المبكر، قبل التعهد بمعالجة السلبيات التي رافقت أداء الفريق في المباريات الأخيرة. وأوضح المدرب عبر مقطع فيديو نشره الموقع الرسمي للنادي، أنه لم يحظ بفرصة كافية لخوض تجارب ودية قبل انطلاقة الموسم للوقوف على إمكانات جميع اللاعبين، خاصة مع انضمام عناصر جديدة خلال فترة الانتقالات الصيفية، مشيرًا إلى أن فترة التوقف الدولي ستساعده في تجهيز الفريق بشكل أفضل. مدرب الهلال يشيد بنجميه كما أشاد زينباور بنجميه سفيان فريد و مصطفى كرشوم ، قائلا: "قدم الحارس سفيان مباراة متميزة، ويعد كرشوم مدافعا رائعا يمتاز بالهدوء والقدرة الفائقة على استخلاص الكرة وبناء اللعب". وأضاف: "تقدمنا مبكرا ولم نستثمر الفرص التي أتيحت لنا، واستقبلنا هدفا في الرمق الأخير من المباراة؛ كان يتعين علينا تسجيل هدفين على الأقل لنحسم المباراة، ولكننا لم نستثمر الفرص، علينا إيجاد حلول لاستقبال الأهداف المتأخرة، وبالمجمل، لست راضيا عن هذه النتيجة". اقرأ أيضًا رامي كمال: الهلال يستحق تكريمًا سياديًا وسنتوج باللقب القاري المريخ يربك تحضيرات الهلال لمجموعات دوري أبطال أفريقيا كما كشف زينباور عن أسباب تذبذب الأداء والتغييرات المستمرة في تشكيل فريقه مؤخرًا، قائلا: "لقد أضفنا عناصر جديدة خلال فترة الانتقالات، لدينا لاعبون شباب نرغب في منحهم فرصة المشاركة؛ لذا نجري هذه التعديلات لنقف على مستوياتهم، ونأمل أن يقدموا الإضافة المرجوة". وأضاف: "واجهنا منافسين أقوياء، على غرار فريق رايون الذي تميز باللياقة العالية والقوة البدنية، وسنواجه تحديات صعبة تستدعي وفرة في العناصر". وختم المدرب الألماني حديثه قائلاً: "نسعى لمزيد من التطور، ويتعين علينا مواصلة العمل الجاد لاستثمار الفرص في تطوير الجوانب البدنية والتكتيكية قبل المباريات الصعبة التي تنتظرنا في دوري أبطال أفريقيا ، إذ يجب أن نستعد جيدا لنبلغ مرحلة متميزة من الجاهزية حتى نتمكن من مجابهة التحديات المرتقبة". النشرة البريدية اشترك المدير الفني للهلال، الألماني جوزيف زينباور، بحسب صحيفة آكشن سبورت، إلى الاعتماد على عناصره الأساسية، رافضاً تكرار تجربة الدفع بتشكيلة يغلب عليها البدلاء، التي كلفت الفريق خسارة ثقيلة أمام مارين football.summary: يستعد الهلال السوداني لمواجهة رايون سبورت الرواندي غداً الأربعاء، في الجولة الثامنة من الدوري الرواندي الممتاز. يسعى الفريق لتعزيز موقعه في جدول الترتيب بعد سلسلة من الانتصارات. المدير الفني جوزيف زينباور، الذي أنهى عقوبة إيقافه، يخطط للاعتماد على تشكيلته الأساسية، رافضاً تكرار تجربة الدفع بالبدلاء التي أدت إلى خسارة ثقيلة أمام مارين. من المتوقع أن يشارك اللاعبون الأساسيون مثل مصطفى كرشوم وياسر عوض وأرنست لوزولو، مع التركيز على الانضباط التكتيكي والتنظيم الدفاعي. تعتبر هذه المباراة اختباراً مهماً للهلال قبل انطلاق دور المجموعات في دوري أبطال أفريقيا، حيث سيواجه حوريا كوناكري الغيني في 28 نوفمبر. تُقام المباراة على ملعب كيغالي بيليه في الساعة السادسة والنصف مساءً، وقد استأنف الهلال تدريباته في كيغالي وسط أجواء من الحماس والتركيز.

football.content: المريخ يربك تحضيرات الهلال لمجموعات دوري أبطال أفريقيا المريخ يربك تحضيرات الهلال لمجموعات دوري أبطال أفريقيا مباريات اليوم من ديربي السودان الكبير بين الغريمين الهلال والمريخ (winwin) 3 نوفمبر 2026 المريخ يربك تحضيرات الهلال لمجموعات دوري أبطال أفريقيا الهلال السوداني المريخ دوري أبطال أفريقيا الدوري السوداني الممتاز كرة قدم حافظ محمد أحمد الخرطوم winwin عاد نجم نادي الهلال والمنتخب السوداني، مصطفى كرشوم، إلى الواجهة بقوة، مقدمًا مستويات مميزة في الآونة الأخيرة، إذ استعاد بريقه الكامل خلال مباراتي "صقور الجديان" في التصفيات الأفريقية، ومباريات فريقه في الدورين التمهيديين لمسابقة دوري أبطال أفريقيا . وقد أشعل المدافع المتألق سباقًا مبكرًا بين قطبي الكرة السودانية مع اقتراب دخوله "الفترة الحرة"، إذ يسعى النادي الأحمر لاستعادة نجمه السابق، بينما يتمسك "الأزرق" بجوهرته بعد أن وجد ضالته في المدافع الفذ، الذي يصنفه الخبراء بأنه أفضل لاعب في البلاد خلال السنوات الأخيرة. الهلال يتحرك للحفاظ على نجمه في هذا السياق، كشفت مصادر موثوقة لموقع "winwin" أن إدارة نادي الهلال استشعرت الخطر، وبدأت تحركاتها مبكرًا لتأمين بقاء نجمها وتمديد تعاقده قبل دخوله الفترة الحرة؛ وذلك بعد أن نجح اللاعب في إعادة الصلابة والهيبة لدفاع الفريق، الذي عانى من تذبذب واضح في مستوياته السابقة. ويعد كرشوم ظاهرة نادرة في الملاعب السودانية؛ نظرًا لسلوكه الاحترافي وانضباطه العالي، فضلًا عن ثبات مستواه وقلة أخطائه. وفي هذا الصدد، فتحت إدارة النادي برئاسة هشام السوباط باب التفاوض مع اللاعب؛ لضمان استمراره في صفوف الفريق لمدة عامين إضافيين على الأقل. اقرأ أيضًا اكتسح الترشيحات.. نجم الهلال السوداني يقترب من تتويج خاص خاص | نجم السودان يفتح النار ويشرح أسباب خيبة المريخ قاريًا وكشفت مصادر عالية الثقة، أنّ إدارة المريخ تعتزم استعادة نجمها، استجابة للمطالبات الجماهيرية الملحة، ونظرًا لقيمته الفنية العالية؛ إذ تعد عودته مكسبًا مضاعفًا باعتباره أفضل مدافع في البلاد، وسيشكل إضافة نوعية للفريق. كما يخدم هذا التوجه خطط إدارة الرئيس مجاهد سهل في التحضير للجمعية العمومية المقررة في مارس 2027 لانتخاب مجلس إدارة جديد، حيث ستحظى الإدارة بدعم كبير إذا نجحت في استعادة كرشوم الذي قدم سنوات مميزة مع الفريق، وأسهم بفاعلية في بلوغه دور المجموعات بدوري أبطال أفريقيا 3 نسخ متتالية. وقد أثارت هذه الرغبة قلق الغريم التقليدي الهلال الذي يستعد بقوة لمرحلة المجموعات. ومن المتوقع أن يحسم اللاعب مستقبله خلال الفترة المقبلة؛ ففي حال تمديد عقده مع ناديه الحالي، ستتلاشى آمال عودته للمريخ مستقبلًا، لا سيما مع بلوغه سن الـ35 عامًا، واقترابه من الاعتزال، أما في حال تعثر مفاوضات التجديد مع الهلال فسيمنح ذلك المريخ الضوء الأخضر لضمه. أخبار ذات صلة الهلال السوداني تحصلا على دعم هائل.. نجما الهلال يواجهان تحديات قارية عنيفة 5 نوفمبر 2026 الهلال السوداني الهلال يتعثر.. ما المكاسب أمام رايون football.summary: تسبب نادي المريخ في إرباك تحضيرات نادي الهلال السوداني لمجموعات دوري أبطال أفريقيا، حيث عاد المدافع مصطفى كرشوم إلى الواجهة بعد تقديمه مستويات مميزة مع منتخب بلاده وناديه. يسعى الهلال للحفاظ على كرشوم، الذي يعتبر من أفضل اللاعبين في السودان، من خلال التفاوض لتمديد عقده قبل دخوله الفترة الحرة. في المقابل، يخطط المريخ لاستعادة نجمه السابق، استجابة لمطالب الجماهير، مما يزيد من حدة المنافسة بين الناديين. كرشوم، الذي ساهم بشكل كبير في نجاح الهلال في السنوات الأخيرة، قد يحسم مستقبله قريبًا. إذا نجح الهلال في تجديد عقده، ستتلاشى آمال المريخ في ضمه، خاصة مع اقتراب اللاعب من الاعتزال. بينما إذا تعثرت المفاوضات، قد يفتح ذلك المجال أمام المريخ لاستعادة خدماته، مما يزيد من التوتر بين الغريمين التقليديين في كرة القدم السودانية.
